title: Non-blocking follow-ups from frontend-position-risk-columns-followups-followups review (PR #259)
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #259 (frontend-position-risk-columns-followups-followups), recorded here so they aren't lost once the PR merges. PR #259 itself was accepted (tests/coverage/lint/type-check all clean, both regression tests independently verified against pre-fix code, browser walkthrough of both fixes confirmed in a real Chromium session).

checklist.step: code-review finding: SellFlaggedPositionsCard.tsx (frontend/src/features/portfolio/components/SellFlaggedPositionsCard.tsx:60) returns null on riskQuery.isError, relying entirely on its sibling RiskSummaryCard (rendered first on DashboardPage, already fully gating its own body on the same failure) to be the page's sole error surface for the shared usePortfolioRisk query. This coupling (SellFlaggedPositionsCard must always be mounted after a component that itself surfaces this exact error) is implicit and unenforced -- nothing stops a future page from mounting SellFlaggedPositionsCard alone or before RiskSummaryCard, in which case a genuine risk-fetch failure would render nothing at all, with no visible error and no console warning. The only regression test (DashboardPage.test.tsx) exercises exactly today's two-siblings-together composition, so it wouldn't catch that regression either. Worth a code comment making the ordering dependency explicit plus a lint/test guard, or a small shared-error-registration helper, if this component is ever reused standalone or reordered.

Broader sweep finding (this review's step 6/PR-level pattern check): the same sibling-duplicate-ErrorState pattern found blocking on PortfolioPage (PR #258, PositionsTable/RiskPanel) and fixed on DashboardPage (this PR, RiskSummaryCard/SellFlaggedPositionsCard) also exists, unfixed, on StockDetailPage: PriceChart, OscillatorChart, VolumeIndicatorsChart, and TrendStrengthChart (all composed together via StockCharts) each call the same useIndicatorHistory(ticker, { range }) hook/query key and each independently renders its own full common/ErrorState on indicatorsQuery.isError. Reproduced with a throwaway test forcing GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators to fail: 4 stacked identical 'Something went wrong' alerts render on the page (confirmed via a one-off vitest run against StockDetailPage, not committed). This is the third occurrence of this exact pattern in the codebase and should be fixed the same way the prior two were -- e.g. only one of the four chart components (most likely PriceChart, which renders first) owns the ErrorState for this specific query's failure, with the other three returning null for it (PriceChart's own separate historyQuery error path is unaffected and should keep rendering as today).

decisions.decision: Fixed SellFlaggedPositionsCard's implicit sibling-ordering coupling with an explicit, caller-supplied `errorSurfacedBySibling` prop (default false) rather than a documented-but-still-implicit ordering invariant (comment + regression test only) or a shared cross-component error-registration helper. On `riskQuery.isError`, the component now renders its own `common/ErrorState` unless the caller explicitly passes `errorSurfacedBySibling`, which `DashboardPage` does (with an inline comment pointing at RiskSummaryCard as the reason). This makes the previous 'nothing stops a future page from mounting this card alone or before RiskSummaryCard' failure mode structurally impossible: a standalone mount (no prop passed) now shows the real error instead of silently rendering nothing, and the suppression only ever happens when a caller has explicitly declared it safe to do so -- independent of render order, so reordering DashboardPage's siblings can no longer break this silently either. Rejected alternatives: (1) a code comment plus a test asserting the current DashboardPage composition, which the task itself flagged as the weaker of the two named options -- it documents the invariant without preventing a future violation of it, and the existing DashboardPage.test.tsx regression test already covers exactly today's composition and would keep passing right through a future ordering break; (2) a shared cross-component error-registration/context helper, which would work but is meaningfully more machinery (a new shared primitive, its own tests, and every future consumer of usePortfolioRisk having to learn it) for a problem an explicit boolean prop already solves cleanly given there are only ever two components sharing this specific query today.
decisions.rationale: Directly closes the task's checklist item 1, which explicitly asked for 'a more robust fix' beyond the ordering-comment approach PR #259 used, giving two example directions (an explicit documented invariant, or an approach that doesn't rely on render order at all) -- the explicit prop satisfies both: it's a literal, type-checked contract at the call site (not just a comment) and it has zero dependency on which sibling actually renders first.

decisions.decision: Fixed the third confirmed sibling-duplicate-ErrorState occurrence (StockCharts' PriceChart/OscillatorChart/VolumeIndicatorsChart/TrendStrengthChart, all sharing useIndicatorHistory) by following the same order-dependent pattern already applied twice (PR #258's PositionsTable/RiskPanel, PR #259's RiskSummaryCard/SellFlaggedPositionsCard), per this checklist item's explicit instruction to do so -- not the explicit-prop approach used for checklist item 1 above. PriceChart (rendered first by StockCharts.tsx) keeps its own `indicatorsQuery.isError` ErrorState unchanged; OscillatorChart/VolumeIndicatorsChart/TrendStrengthChart now render nothing for that same failure, each with an inline comment naming PriceChart as the shared failure's sole owner. PriceChart's own separate `historyQuery` error path is untouched. Updated each of the three suppressed components' own standalone-error tests (404/503/422 cases previously asserting an alert) to assert the new silent-degrade behavior instead, and added a StockCharts.test.tsx page-level regression test asserting exactly one alert renders when all four charts are mounted together and GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators fails -- the same page-level-regression-test pattern PortfolioPage.test.tsx/DashboardPage.test.tsx already established for the first two occurrences, since a standalone per-component test can't catch a duplicate that only appears once all four are mounted together.
decisions.rationale: The checklist item's own wording ('follow the same fix pattern already applied twice before... check those diffs for precedent') is a direct instruction to replicate the existing order-dependent pattern here, not to re-litigate its robustness -- that concern was deliberately scoped to checklist item 1's SellFlaggedPositionsCard fix only. Not applying the same explicit-prop treatment to these three chart components here also keeps this PR's diff focused and consistent with precedent; if the render-order coupling on StockCharts is later judged to need the same robustness treatment as SellFlaggedPositionsCard, that is exactly the kind of finding a future PR review of this task's PR would surface as its own follow-up task, the same way this task itself originated as a followup of PR #259's review.

comments.summary: SellFlaggedPositionsCard's new errorSurfacedBySibling prop fails safe: default false, so a standalone/future mount with no prop passed shows the real ErrorState instead of silently rendering nothing. Verified via diff read, the updated SellFlaggedPositionsCard.test.tsx (both the default-shows-error and errorSurfacedBySibling=true-suppresses-error cases), and a live browser walkthrough of DashboardPage with GET /api/portfolio/risk mocked to fail (exactly one alert rendered, from RiskSummaryCard; SellFlaggedPositionsCard's whole section absent as intended).

StockCharts.test.tsx's new regression test genuinely would have failed pre-fix: reproduced by checking out the pre-fix commit (7f8714e) in a scratch worktree, copying the new test file in, and running it against the old OscillatorChart/VolumeIndicatorsChart/TrendStrengthChart -- it failed with 3 alerts instead of 1, confirming the test is a real regression guard and not a tautology.

Live browser walkthrough of StockDetailPage with GET /api/stocks/AAPL/indicators mocked to fail confirmed exactly one 'Something went wrong' ErrorState (owned by PriceChart, rendered first in StockCharts.tsx) and the Oscillators/Volume Indicators/Trend Strength sections rendering only their section headers with nothing beneath (no duplicate alert, no stray loading/empty state). Confirmed via grep that only StockCharts.tsx currently imports these three chart components, so today's hard-coded 'PriceChart owns this failure' assumption holds in practice, even though it's not enforced the same order-independent way SellFlaggedPositionsCard's fix is (see non-blocking finding below, tracked as a followup per this task's own decisions entry expecting exactly this kind of finding).

Non-blocking (tracked as frontend-position-risk-columns-followups-followups-followups-followups): PriceChart's own indicatorsQuery.isError ErrorState is gated behind showOverlaySection (historyQuery.isSuccess && hasBars && overlayEnabled), a pre-existing condition unrelated to error ownership. If historyQuery itself fails or returns zero usable bars while indicatorsQuery also fails, none of the four StockCharts components now surface the indicators failure specifically (previously the three suppressed siblings would have shown their own independent ErrorState in that compound-failure scenario) -- a real, if narrow, regression introduced by this PR's unconditional suppression. Independently corroborated by a parallel code-review pass run during this review.

Non-blocking (tracked as frontend-position-risk-columns-followups-followups-followups-followups): OscillatorChart/VolumeIndicatorsChart/TrendStrengthChart's suppression of their own ErrorState is a hard-coded, unconditional assumption that PriceChart is always mounted as a sibling and owns this failure, not an opt-in/order-independent contract the way SellFlaggedPositionsCard's errorSurfacedBySibling prop is. This is a deliberate, documented scope decision (this task's own decisions entry explicitly limited the more-robust treatment to checklist item 1 per the checklist item's own wording), and only StockCharts.tsx currently uses these three components, so there's no live bug today -- but the same coupling-fragility class this PR fixed once (for SellFlaggedPositionsCard) is knowingly left in place a second time.

review.notes: Full review: backend pytest --cov=app (1144 passed, 99.95% coverage, unaffected by this PR) and frontend vitest run --coverage (767 passed, 99.74%/99.23%/99.75%/99.8% statements/branches/functions/lines, well above the 90% gate) both green. Backend ruff/mypy and frontend eslint/tsc all clean; scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py clean. code-review skill run in parallel corroborated both non-blocking findings below independently. Live browser walkthrough (Playwright via a scratch Node script, since chromium-cli wasn't available in this environment) covered the golden path (Dashboard and StockDetailPage(AAPL) normal loads) and both PR's edge cases (GET /api/portfolio/risk failing, GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators failing) -- no console errors beyond the intentionally-mocked 500s, no unexpected network failures. e2e-test skill (make e2e) run separately: all 21 specs across 4 files (dashboard, navigation, portfolio, stock-analysis, watchlist) passed. Both decisions entries are well-reasoned and each closes its checklist item; no checklist item was phrased as 'decide X' without a corresponding decision. Two non-blocking findings (both on the StockCharts side of the fix, none on SellFlaggedPositionsCard) filed as a followup task rather than only left as PR comments, per CLAUDE.md's tracked-followup rule.

pr_decision.notes: Re-ran both suites independently: backend pytest --cov=app 1144 passed/99.95% coverage, frontend vitest run --coverage 767 passed/99.74%-99.8% statements-branches-functions-lines -- both match pr-reviewer's numbers exactly; frontend eslint/tsc clean; backend ruff shows 7 pre-existing findings in unrelated test files, confirmed present on origin/main too via a throwaway worktree (backend untouched by this PR's diff, not a regression). Read the full diff. Specifically reproduced the flagged compound-failure gap with two throwaway vitest scenarios against StockCharts: (1) GET .../history and GET .../indicators both 500 -> exactly one alert renders (PriceChart's own historyQuery ErrorState, detail 'history boom'), no indicators-specific message but not zero indication either; (2) GET .../history succeeds with zero bars (all filtered by hasFiniteOhlc) while GET .../indicators 500s -> PriceChart shows only its 'No price history available' EmptyState (no alert), and Oscillator/Volume/TrendStrength charts render nothing beneath their headers -- confirmed this is a real, narrow regression versus pre-PR behavior (verified via `git diff 98a4697^ 98a4697` that the three sibling charts previously rendered their own ungated ErrorState here). Concur with pr-reviewer's non-blocking classification: PriceChart.tsx itself (where the showOverlaySection gate lives) was not touched by this PR -- that gate predates it -- this PR only changed the three siblings' own indicatorsQuery.isError handling per the checklist item's explicit instruction to replicate existing precedent; the scenario requires two independent endpoints failing/degrading simultaneously; the page never renders a blank void indistinguishable from normal operation (always shows either an alert or an explicit EmptyState); and the gap is already filed with full reproduction detail and proposed remedies as frontend-position-risk-columns-followups-followups-followups-followups (state: planned), satisfying the tracked-followup rule. Also verified SellFlaggedPositionsCard's errorSurfacedBySibling prop defaults to false (fail-safe) and both task decisions entries genuinely close their checklist items.
